bringup-o.id-register-s: 9Fh Read Identification (manufacturer ID, memory type, capacity); 90h Manufacturer/Device ID
bringup-o.check-s: 05h Read Status Register: WIP = 0 when idle; QE (S9) is 0 as delivered (Status Register 00h), so quad reads need QE written to 1 first (non-volatile)
bringup-o.source-s: GD25LQ128E Rev1.1: ID table p20; 8.2 Initial Delivery State p46 (Status Register 00h, all bits 0); QE bit S9 non-volatile p14-15

component-o.description-s: 128 Mbit 1.8 V serial NOR flash, standard / dual / quad SPI and QPI, 120 MHz, 1.65 V to 2.0 V, -40 to 85 C, SOP8 208 mil, tape and reel. Delivered with QE = 0. The 100 nF VCC decoupling in stdpins-ao is common practice, not a datasheet value

cfgpins-ao.1c: CS# must not be selected before tVSL (2.5 ms after VCC min, Table 12 p46); a pull-up holds it deselected while the host pin floats. Value not given, 10k used as for the W25Q128JW it replaces.

cfgpins-ao.3c: Write protect while QE = 0 (as delivered), IO2 once QE = 1. Wire to the host's IO2; until firmware sets QE, the host must hold it high (or a pull-up must). Pull-up 10k to VCC (value not given by the datasheet; common practice) so WP# reads high while QE = 0 and the host pin is not yet driven.

cfgpins-ao.7c: Hold while QE = 0 (as delivered), IO3 once QE = 1. Wire to the host's IO3; until firmware sets QE, HOLD# low pauses the device, so the host must hold it high (or a pull-up must). Unlike W25Q128JWSIQ (QE = 1 from the factory), quad mode needs a one-time QE write. Pull-up 10k to VCC (value not given by the datasheet; common practice) so HOLD# reads high while QE = 0.

component-o.replaces_s: W25Q128JWSIQ (Winbond, 3 at DigiKey, 0 at Mouser): same SOP8 208 mil pinout and 1.8 V quad SPI; QE = 0 as delivered (Winbond IQ: QE = 1), 120 MHz vs 133 MHz, JEDEC ID C8 60 18 vs EF 60 18

step_source-o.derived-s: derived: operating max 20 mA (p48) less the smallest low-power current 0.001 mA (p48, ICC2 Deep Power-Down Current CS#=VCC, VIN=VCC or VSS)
